metadata.description: Primary sources for specification, model checking, refinement, SMT interpretation, tool selection, industrial evidence, and LLM-generated spec/proof benchmarks.
metadata.title: Formal Methods Foundations — Primary Sources

sources.name: Specifying Systems
sources.description: Author-hosted book. Chapter 2 defines behaviors/specification; chapters 5 and 8 address invariance, implementation, liveness/fairness and refinement; chapter 14 addresses TLC model checking. Supports conceptual guidance, not a claim that this small helper implements TLA+.

sources.name: SMT-LIB language documentation
sources.description: Official language reference and links to its specification. Supports distinguishing an encoded satisfiability query from a general implementation claim; no runtime version pin is prescribed.

sources.name: Newcombe et al., How Amazon Web Services Uses Formal Methods (CACM 58(4), 2015)
sources.description: Industrial TLA+ evidence. Figures used in tool-selection.md (10 systems, 7 teams, 2-3 weeks to useful results, 35-step DynamoDB trace, missed liveness bug, 'we don't' know code matches design, Alloy expressiveness in 2014) were read in the authors' 2014 technical-report text; CACM metadata verified via dblp/ACM listing.

sources.name: Brooker & Desai, Systems Correctness Practices at Amazon Web Services (CACM 2025; ACM Queue 10.1145/3712057)
sources.description: Abstract-level scope only: model checking, fuzzing, PBT, fault injection, deterministic and event-based simulation, runtime trace validation; specs as test oracles. Full text not read; quote no figures from it. Crossref confirms DOI 10.1145/3729175 (CACM, 2025) and 10.1145/3712057 (ACM Queue), both Brooker and Desai.

sources.name: P language case studies
sources.description: P used across AWS storage, database and compute teams; PObserve validates structured service logs against P specifications post hoc.

sources.name: Disselkoen et al., How We Built Cedar: A Verification-Guided Approach (arXiv:2407.01688)
sources.description: Verification-guided development: executable model with proofs, differential random testing, PBT; proofs found 4 validator bugs, DRT/PBT 21 more (abstract).

sources.name: Ye et al., VERINA: Benchmarking Verifiable Code Generation (arXiv:2505.23135 v3, 2026-03-16)
sources.description: 189 Lean tasks; best model o3: 72.6% code correctness, 52.3% spec soundness/completeness, 4.9% proof success, one trial per task (abstract of v3).

sources.name: Bursuc et al., A benchmark for vericoding: formally verified program synthesis (arXiv:2509.22908)
sources.description: 12,504 specs; vericoding success 27% Lean, 44% Verus/Rust, 82% Dafny with off-the-shelf LLMs; pure Dafny verification 68% to 96% over a year (abstract).

sources.name: TLA+ tools (TLC, PlusCal translator, SANY)
sources.description: TLC explicit-state model checker; worked example checked with tla2tools.jar 'Version 2.19 of 08 August 2024' on 2026-09-23.

sources.name: Apalache symbolic model checker for TLA+
sources.description: Translates TLA+ to SMT (Z3); bounded model checking and inductive checks; backend for Quint.

sources.name: Quint specification language
sources.description: Engineer-friendly syntax for TLA-style specs; uses Apalache as backend.

sources.name: P programming language
sources.description: State-machine modeling language with schedule-based P Checker testing, PEx exhaustive exploration, and PObserve trace checking. Before making a coverage claim, read https://p-org.github.io/P/getstarted/usingP/ and https://p-org.github.io/P/advanced/pex/; distinguish configured schedule exploration from a completed exhaustive search.

sources.name: Alloy 6 release notes
sources.description: Alloy 6 adds mutable signatures/fields (var), linear-time temporal logic with past operators, and NuSMV/nuXmv backends.

sources.name: Z3 theorem prover
sources.description: SMT solver; sat/unsat/unknown semantics.

sources.name: cvc5 SMT solver
sources.description: SMT solver.

sources.name: Kani Rust Verifier
sources.description: Bounded model checker for Rust.

sources.name: CBMC bounded model checker
sources.description: Bounded model checker for C/C++.

sources.name: Dafny
sources.description: Verification-aware programming language.

sources.name: Verus
sources.description: Verified Rust for low-level systems code.

sources.name: Lean 4
sources.description: Proof assistant and programming language.

sources.name: The Rocq Prover (formerly Coq)
sources.description: Site states Rocq was formerly known as the Coq Proof Assistant.

sources.name: Isabelle
sources.description: Generic proof assistant (Isabelle/HOL).
